# integrity/new-suppression

Suppression added in the change.

A new `ubon-ignore` comment or a new entry in `.ubon/baseline.json`. Every one is listed with the rule it suppresses and the reason given.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: warn by default; block when ubon.json sets `"suppressions": { "agent": "human-only" }` and the check runs for an agent session.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.

## Why it matters

A suppression turns a finding off on the word of whoever wrote it. Listing each new one keeps a suppression written by an agent visible to the person who reviews the change.

## Not flagged

- the secret/db-url-password entry existed at the base
- suppressions.agent is human-only, but this check is not an agent session, so new entries warn instead of blocking
- `export const testKey = 'pk_test_placeholder';` in `lib/payments.ts`: this suppression existed at the base; it only moved below charge()
- `export const other = 'your-api-key-here';` in `lib/payments.ts`: an ubon-ignore without a reason suppresses nothing (integrity/invalid-suppression reports it)
- `export const help = 'Write // ubon-ignore <rule>: <who>: <evidence> above the line.';` in `lib/payments.ts`: the syntax inside a string is not a suppression
- `export const staging = 'https://staging.example.com';` in `src/config.ts`: this suppression was approved before the session started

## How to fix

Check that the reason is true and remove the suppression if the finding is real.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore integrity/new-suppression: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "integrity/new-suppression": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
